defiscan.label: Stage 0
defiscan.verbatim: Stage 0. Spark is a protocol within the Sky ecosystem and consists of two main products: _Savings USDS_ and _SparkLend_. _Savings USDS_ is a savings product offering a fixed return on various stablecoins including `USDS`, `DAI` and `USDC`. _SparkLend_ is a lending protocol that enables users to lend and borrow various crypto assets. It offers deep stablecoin liquidity that is provided to a large part by Sky through Spark's _Liquidity Management Layer_. Spark's _Liquidity Management Layer_ allocates Sky stablecoin liquidity to various DeFi lending markets including _SparkLend_. The focus in this review is thus on its role within _SparkLend_ itself.

keyFindings.title: 13 Unverified Core Contracts Block Source Auditing
keyFindings.description: 22% of discovered contracts lack verified source on block explorers. Unverified targets include SparkLend PoolConfigurator (reserve/oracle config), KillSwitchOracle, spETH vault proxy, Spark Savings Intents, Optimism Token Bridge proxy, SparkLend Freezer multisig shell, and all L2 Spark Executors / ALM Controllers on Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, and Unichain plus Gnosis Pool. Without verified bytecode-to-source mapping, privileged upgrade paths, oracle logic, and cross-chain execution cannot be independently confirmed despite GitHub references and prior audits.

keyFindings.title: Unverified PoolConfigurator Controls SparkLend Reserve Parameters
keyFindings.description: PoolConfigurator proxy at 0x542DBa469bdE58FAeE189ffB60C6b49CE60E0738 is a core SparkLend contract responsible for reserve initialization, collateral parameters, interest rate strategies, and pause/freeze flags. It is deployed behind an Aave-style proxy with upgrade authority flowing through PoolAddressesProvider (owned by SubProxy), but the implementation source is not Etherscan-verified, preventing confirmation that deployed bytecode matches audited Aave v3 fork patches.

keyFindings.title: Unverified L2 ALM Controllers Hold Cross-Chain Capital
keyFindings.description: ForeignController ALM instances on Arbitrum (0x689502…06f7 on Optimism, 0xF16DE7…D5bA on Unichain, plus Arbitrum/Base entries in registry) are unverified despite controlling rate-limited DeFi deployments via ALM Proxy. Verified ForeignController source on Arbitrum (0xC40611…) shows RELAYER/FREEZER AccessControl and nonReentrant guards, but unverified deployments cannot be confirmed to match audited bytecode.

keyFindings.title: Unverified Cross-Chain Executors and Gov Relays
keyFindings.description: Spark Executor on Arbitrum (0x65d946…f7a1), Base (0xF93B71…F579), and Sky Gov Relay on Base (0xdD0BCc…C255) lack verified source. These contracts receive L1 governance messages and delegatecall into L2 targets. Arbitrum PSM3 (0x2B05F8…7266) is also unverified. Cross-chain spell execution is a high-privilege path; unverified executors create governance asymmetry versus fully verified mainnet SubProxy stack.

keyFindings.title: SparkLend Core Uses Immutable-Admin Proxies Upgradable by SubProxy
keyFindings.description: Pool (0xC13e21…) and PoolConfigurator deploy as InitializableImmutableAdminUpgradeabilityProxy instances whose admin is PoolAddressesProvider. On-chain, PoolAddressesProvider.owner()=SubProxy (0x3300f198…8c4). SubProxy can upgrade Pool/Configurator implementations, set oracles, ACLManager, and sentinel addresses via onlyOwner functions—concentrating upgrade authority in Maker-style governance rather than SPK token voting.

keyFindings.title: SubProxy Delegatecall Enables Arbitrary Target Execution
keyFindings.description: SubProxy.exec(target, args) performs delegatecall into any target for addresses with wards. Verified on-chain wards are held by Sky Pause Proxy (0xBE8E3e36…) and Spark StarGuard (0x6605aa12…). While StarGuard enforces a 7-day maxDelay for whitelisted spells, SubProxy itself has no on-chain timelock—compromise of a ward holder enables immediate execution of arbitrary delegatecall payloads against any authorized target.

keyFindings.title: ALM Proxy Grants Controller Arbitrary External and Delegate Calls
keyFindings.description: ALMProxy (verified) exposes doCall, doCallWithValue, and doDelegateCall restricted to CONTROLLER role. MainnetController holds this role and can route capital through Aave, Curve, CCTP, LayerZero, PSM, and other integrations. ALMProxyFreezable adds FREEZER role to revoke controllers. Compromise of a RELAYER key or governance spell error could move funds across integrated protocols within rate-limit bounds.

keyFindings.title: Executive Control via Sky Parent, Not SPK Holders
keyFindings.description: On-chain verification shows SubProxy wards are held by Sky Pause Proxy (0xBE8E3e36…) and Spark StarGuard (0x6605aa12…), not SPK token holders. SubProxy owns PoolAddressesProvider, is ACL admin, holds POOL_ADMIN and EMERGENCY_ADMIN on ACLManager, and DEFAULT_ADMIN on ALM MainnetController. SPK governance is off-chain Snapshot signaling; execution requires Sky Atlas updates and executive spells.

keyFindings.title: No Timelock on SubProxy Direct Execution
keyFindings.description: SubProxy.exec() performs immediate delegatecall execution for any address with wards. While StarGuard enforces a 7-day maxDelay for whitelisted proxy spells, the SubProxy contract itself has no built-in timelock. Sky Pause Proxy can authorize and execute changes without an on-chain delay at the SubProxy layer.

keyFindings.title: Unverified Arbitrum Spark Executor
keyFindings.description: Cross-chain governance on Arbitrum routes L1 SubProxy messages through ArbitrumReceiver (l1Authority=SubProxy) to Spark Executor 0x65d946…f7a1, which is unverified on-chain. This creates a governance asymmetry: mainnet contracts are verified and auditable, but the primary Arbitrum execution target cannot be source-audited.

keyFindings.title: Extreme Supply Concentration in Protocol-Controlled Wallets
keyFindings.description: On-chain balanceOf queries (June 2026) show top protocol addresses hold ~78% of total supply: Sky Pause Proxy 5.13B (51.4%), team/subDAO proxy 1.24B (12.4%), long-term treasury 600M (6.0%), stSPK vault 570M (5.7%), mid-term treasury 185M (1.9%), airdrops-legacy 61M (0.6%). Top-10 holder analysis (CoinLore/Etherscan) confirms ~89% held by top 10 addresses, overwhelmingly treasuries and vesting contracts—not retail distribution despite '65% to users' marketing framing.

keyFindings.title: Aggressive Year 1–2 Farming Emissions
keyFindings.description: Sky Atlas farming schedule releases 1.625B SPK/year in years 1–2 (32.5% of total supply over 2 years), halving in subsequent biennial periods. On-chain farming reserve dropped from 6.5B to 5.13B, confirming ~1.37B already distributed. Against ~2.5B circulating supply, annualized farming inflation is ~65% in year 2—well above typical DeFi governance tokens and a sustained sell-pressure source unless demand absorbs emissions.
